items.corrected_text: A municipal factsheet on parking counts of 3, 5 and 6 October 2019 reports that the three municipal garages (Centraal, Musis, Rozet; 2,190 spaces combined) were full at the same time on Saturday afternoon 5 October, between about 12:00 and 16:00, and that on average 72 percent of street spaces in the research area (the centre between the Singels and the Rijn) were occupied at that peak. Paid street parking cost EUR 2.90 per hour at that time, and on Thursday evenings the garage tariff after 18:00 was EUR 0.50 per hour.

Prinsenhof forecourt); about 73% of street spaces occupied at the busiest moment (Saturday afternoon); on Saturday afternoon all municipal garages full in 2020 and 2021; Musis quick wins on floors ground to +1 total EUR 510,000; PBA proposes to reserve EUR 350,000. Topic label 'demand' is weak (this is bicycle parking supply) but the facts hold.

Opened the PDF. Proposal dated 30 Sep 2025 (B&W proposal; the council decision block is blank). Confirmed: first resident permit outside the centre free; underground garage inside the centrumring to be studied (motion 25M61); town hall garage too small for profitable exploitation; EUR 2.9 million credit for parking machines. Too strong: the text says 'Het straatparkeren in de binnenstad willen we geleidelijk afbouwen' (we want to gradually scale back), stated as an aim, not a commitment to phase out/eliminate it; also the policy document itself was not part of the PDF.
items.corrected_text: On 30 September 2025 the municipality proposed to the council a Parkeerbeleid Arnhem 2025. It states a wish to gradually scale back street parking in the centre, to study an (underground) parking garage inside the centrumring and to make the first resident permit outside the centre free. It judged the town hall garage too small to run profitably as a public garage and asked for a EUR 2.9 million credit for new parking machines; the council's vote is not shown in the document.

items.corrected_text: The city executive adopted the Nota Parkeernormen Arnhem 2026 on 17 March 2026; the regulation page shows it valid from 26 March 2026. It adds an A+ area covering the inner city and the Arnhem Centraal station area, where new housing can be exempt from building car parking provided alternatives, mainly bicycle parking, are realised, and no parking permits are issued for exempt developments. In A and B areas the norms become maxima as well as minima, with the A norms set 20 percent below current car ownership (B 10 percent); average car ownership in Arnhem was 0.82 cars per household in 2023.

items.note: Opened the Omroep Gelderland page, dated 13 May (updated 14 May), no year on the page (2026 inferred from the weekday pattern of 15-17 May and the footer). The article was written before the shows, so 'drew' and 'ran' are too strong. items.corrected_text: On 13 May 2026, Omroep Gelderland reported that Suzan & Freek would play ten sold-out shows at GelreDome from 15 May, with room for tens of thousands of fans per show. Parking at the lots at GelreDome, Kronenburg, Gelderse Poort and Papendal required a pre-bought parking ticket, shuttle buses were arranged from several lots, and shuttle buses were to run from Arnhem Centraal (about 10 minutes, EUR 5.90 return). On many dates a large part of the parking tickets was already sold out.

corrected_summary: Arnhem is moving towards fewer cars in the centre and higher parking prices. In a proposal of 30 September 2025 the municipality said it wants to gradually scale back street parking in the centre, to study an underground garage inside the centrumring and to make the first resident permit outside the centre free; the council's vote on it was not found. The Nota Parkeernormen Arnhem 2026, adopted by the city executive on 17 March 2026 and valid from 26 March, adds an A+ area (inner city and station area) where new housing can be exempt from building car parking if alternatives such as bicycle parking are provided. New rules for an environmental zone for diesel cars and buses and a zero-emission zone for vans and trucks have applied in the centre since 1 June 2026. Since 1 January 2026 street parking costs EUR 4.60 per hour in the centre and several surrounding districts and EUR 3.10 elsewhere. The June 2026 coalition agreement plans parking to become 30 cents per hour more expensive on top of inflation, and the September 2026 financial plans point to rises of 2.1 percent a year plus 90 cents per hour in total, with street parking in and around the centre heading towards EUR 6 per hour; both are plans, not tariffs in force. The three municipal garages (Centraal, Musis, Rozet) share one tariff of EUR 0.70 per 10 minutes by day (06:00 to 18:00), EUR 1.70 per hour in the evening and night and a maximum of EUR 24 per day. Q-Park Broerenstraat (426 spaces) and the private Velperplein garage add supply, and the P+R sites at GelreDome and Arnhem Zuid are free apart from the public transport fare. Municipal counts in October 2019 found the three municipal garages (2,190 spaces combined) full at the same time on a Saturday afternoon, and the municipality reported them full on Saturday afternoon again in 2020 and 2021. Ahead of ten sold-out concerts at GelreDome from 15 May 2026, Omroep Gelderland reported that parking at the lots near the stadium required a pre-bought ticket and that shuttle buses were arranged.
